title: Tool calling is a proposal–execution loop
outcome: Follow tool arguments, host execution, call IDs, and results without giving the model unrestricted access.
cue: The model asks. The host validates and runs.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Follow tool arguments, host execution, call IDs, and results without giving the model unrestricted access.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: Schema-valid arguments can still be unauthorized. A tool can return injected instructions. A timeout after a write can have an unknown outcome, so a blind retry can duplicate effects.

trace.title: Declared tools
trace.detail:
The model can emit a request to use a declared tool. In a client-side integration, your host application receives that proposal, validates it, executes permitted code, and returns a tool result. The model does not obtain the function's privileges merely by generating its name.

A tool definition describes name, purpose, and argument shape. Keep descriptions narrow and schemas small. Resolve identity outside arguments. Treat arguments as outside input and results as potentially untrusted content. Return bounded data with explicit errors.

The host maintains the conversation item linking a call ID to its result. A second model step can use the result to answer or propose another call. Put limits on steps, time, output size, and total cost. Some platforms can execute tools server-side; their execution boundary and authorization still need an explicit design.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: User input → model tool proposal → schema and policy checks → bounded function → safe result with matching call ID → model continuation. Trace the real tool name, duration, result status, and policy decision without logging private arguments by default.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Schema-valid arguments can still be unauthorized. A tool can return injected instructions. A timeout after a write can have an unknown outcome, so a blind retry can duplicate effects.
